title: A better life
paragraphs: How are you feeling today? Often when we ask people that question, they reply ‘not bad’, or ‘could be worse’. But what would make us feel ‘perfect’? Maybe we could live better by being healthier, less stressed, more motivated – but how?

Of course there are many remedies for improving our mental health, but sometimes there are small and simple solutions to help improve our wellbeing. It’s something the BBC TV programme Easy Ways to Live Well has been looking at. It suggested several ‘health hacks’ which the programme’s presenters tried and gave their ‘seal of approval’. And maybe they could help us too.

Firstly, to tackle putting on weight and to cut the calories, the programme found sniffing peppermint stops our craving for a snack. Presenter, chef and writer Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall says “a scientific theory called ‘mutual competition’ shows that a strong smell can distract our brain from the food we’re thinking about.”

If your addiction to your smartphone is getting you down, it’s suggested that turning your phone screen grey helps you reduce screen time because a black and white screen becomes less attractive to look at. With recent studies showing our phones can make us 26% less productive and increase our stress, it seems like a no-brainer to try this ‘dim’ idea.

Fancy a swim in ice-cold water? Well, the BBC programme found a daily dip in freezing water gets you used to the stress of doing it and therefore prepares you for other life stresses. And another way to ‘chill out’ is to leave your smartphone at home, immerse yourself in a forest, and breathe in the fresh air. Forest bathing is the perfect tonic for the stresses of urban life.

Other life-improving ideas included things such as singing to reduce pain and fidgeting more to get away from our sedentary lives. But whatever therapy we choose to adopt, it seems any change to our lifestyle can help improve our body and mind.

vocabulary.entry: wellbeing /ˈwelbiːɪŋ/ n. 健康；幸福感
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet and regular exercise are essential for wellbeing.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡饮食和规律运动对身心健康至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: remedy /ˈremədi/ n. 方法；补救措施
vocabulary.example: Laughter is a good remedy for stress.
vocabulary.translation: 笑是缓解压力的好方法。

vocabulary.entry: health hack /ˈhelθ hæk/ n. 健康小窍门
vocabulary.example: This health hack helps you fall asleep faster at night.
vocabulary.translation: 这个健康小窍门能帮你晚上更快入睡。

vocabulary.entry: seal of approval /siːl ɒv əˈpruːvl/ 认可；批准
vocabulary.example: The product has received the seal of approval from leading experts.
vocabulary.translation: 该产品已获得权威专家的认可。

vocabulary.entry: tackle /ˈtækl/ v. 应对；处理
vocabulary.example: We need to tackle the problem of pollution immediately.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要立即着手解决污染问题。

vocabulary.entry: cut the calories /kʌt ðə ˈkælərɪz/ 减少热量摄入
vocabulary.example: Eating more vegetables is an easy way to cut the calories.
vocabulary.translation: 多吃蔬菜是减少热量摄入的简单方法。

vocabulary.entry: sniff /snɪf/ v. 嗅；闻
vocabulary.example: She bent down to sniff the flowers in the garden.
vocabulary.translation: 她弯腰去闻花园里的花。

vocabulary.entry: peppermint /ˈpepəmɪnt/ n. 薄荷
vocabulary.example: Peppermint tea can help with digestion.
vocabulary.translation: 薄荷茶有助于消化。

vocabulary.entry: craving /ˈkreɪvɪŋ/ n. 渴望；渴求
vocabulary.example: She has a craving for chocolate when she’s tired.
vocabulary.translation: 她累的时候就特别想吃巧克力。

vocabulary.entry: mutual competition /ˈmjuːtʃuəl ˌkɒmpəˈtɪʃn/ 相互竞争
vocabulary.example: Mutual competition between the two teams made the game exciting.
vocabulary.translation: 两队之间的相互竞争让比赛变得很精彩。

vocabulary.entry: distract /dɪˈstrækt/ v. 分散注意力；使分心
vocabulary.example: The noise outside distracted me from my work.
vocabulary.translation: 外面的噪音让我无法专心工作。

vocabulary.entry: addiction /əˈdɪkʃn/ n. 沉迷；上瘾
vocabulary.example: His addiction to computer games affected his studies.
vocabulary.translation: 他沉迷电脑游戏，影响了学习。

vocabulary.entry: get you down /ɡet juː daʊn/ 使你沮丧；让你心情低落
vocabulary.example: Don’t let the bad news get you down.
vocabulary.translation: 别让坏消息让你心情低落。

vocabulary.entry: no-brainer /ˌnəʊ ˈbreɪnə(r)/ n. 无需思考的事；明智的选择
vocabulary.example: Choosing this affordable hotel was a no-brainer.
vocabulary.translation: 选择这家经济实惠的酒店是个明智的决定。

vocabulary.entry: dip /dɪp/ n. 浸泡；短暂的游泳
vocabulary.example: She took a quick dip in the lake on a hot day.
vocabulary.translation: 大热天里她在湖里快速游了一会儿。

vocabulary.entry: freezing /ˈfriːzɪŋ/ adj. 极冷的；冰冻的
vocabulary.example: The freezing weather made the roads icy.
vocabulary.translation: 严寒的天气让路面结了冰。

vocabulary.entry: chill out /tʃɪl aʊt/ 放松；冷静下来
vocabulary.example: We need to chill out after a busy week at work.
vocabulary.translation: 忙碌的一周工作过后，我们需要放松一下。

vocabulary.entry: immerse /ɪˈmɜːs/ v. 使沉浸在；使深陷于
vocabulary.example: She immersed herself in her studies and forgot the time.
vocabulary.translation: 她沉浸在学习中，忘记了时间。

vocabulary.entry: forest bathing /ˈfɒrɪst ˈbeɪðɪŋ/ 森林浴
vocabulary.example: Forest bathing is popular in Japan for its health benefits.
vocabulary.translation: 森林浴在日本很受欢迎，因为它对健康有益。

vocabulary.entry: tonic /ˈtɒnɪk/ n. 补药；有滋补作用的事物
vocabulary.example: A walk in the fresh air is a wonderful tonic for the mind.
vocabulary.translation: 在新鲜空气中散步是极好的精神滋补品。

vocabulary.entry: fidget /ˈfɪdʒɪt/ v. 坐立不安；不停摆弄
vocabulary.example: He tends to fidget when he’s nervous.
vocabulary.translation: 他紧张的时候就会坐立不安。

vocabulary.entry: sedentary /ˈsedntri/ adj. 久坐的；缺乏运动的
vocabulary.example: A sedentary lifestyle can lead to various health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 久坐的生活方式会引发多种健康问题。

sentences.english: Often when we ask people that question, they reply ‘not bad’, or ‘could be worse’.
sentences.chinese: 当我们问别人这个问题时，得到的回答往往是“还不错”或者“不算太糟”。

sentences.english: But what would make us feel ‘perfect’?
sentences.chinese: 但什么才能让我们感觉“完美”呢？

sentences.english: Maybe we could live better by being healthier, less stressed, more motivated – but how?
sentences.chinese: 或许更健康的身体、更小的压力、更足的干劲能让生活变得更好——但具体该怎么做呢？

sentences.english: Of course there are many remedies for improving our mental health, but sometimes there are small and simple solutions to help improve our wellbeing.
sentences.chinese: 改善心理健康的方法当然有很多，但有时候一些微小又简单的办法就能帮我们提升幸福感。

sentences.english: It’s something the BBC TV programme Easy Ways to Live Well has been looking at. It suggested several ‘health hacks’ which the programme’s presenters tried and gave their ‘seal of approval’.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司的电视节目《健康生活小妙招》就关注了这类方法，节目推荐了几个“健康小窍门”，主持人亲自试过之后都给予了认可。

sentences.english: And maybe they could help us too.
sentences.chinese: 或许这些方法也能帮到我们。

sentences.english: Firstly, to tackle putting on weight and to cut the calories, the programme found sniffing peppermint stops our craving for a snack.
sentences.chinese: 首先，针对体重增加和热量摄入的问题，节目发现闻薄荷的气味能抑制我们想吃零食的欲望。

sentences.english: Presenter, chef and writer Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall says “a scientific theory called ‘mutual competition’ shows that a strong smell can distract our brain from the food we’re thinking about.”
sentences.chinese: 主持人、同时也是厨师和作家的休·费恩利-惠廷斯托尔表示：“有一种名为‘相互竞争’的科学理论认为，强烈的气味会分散大脑的注意力，让我们不再想着那些想吃的食物。”

sentences.english: If your addiction to your smartphone is getting you down, it’s suggested that turning your phone screen grey helps you reduce screen time because a black and white screen becomes less attractive to look at.
sentences.chinese: 如果你因为沉迷手机而心情低落，不妨试试把手机屏幕调成灰色，这能帮你减少看手机的时间，因为黑白屏幕的吸引力会大大下降。

sentences.english: With recent studies showing our phones can make us 26% less productive and increase our stress, it seems like a no-brainer to try this ‘dim’ idea.
sentences.chinese: 近期研究表明，手机会让我们的工作效率降低26%，还会增加压力，所以试试这个“昏暗”的办法显然是明智之举。

sentences.english: Fancy a swim in ice-cold water?
sentences.chinese: 想试试在冰水里游泳吗？

sentences.english: Well, the BBC programme found a daily dip in freezing water gets you used to the stress of doing it and therefore prepares you for other life stresses.
sentences.chinese: 英国广播公司的节目发现，每天泡一泡冰水能让身体适应这种压力，从而为应对生活中的其他压力做好准备。

sentences.english: And another way to ‘chill out’ is to leave your smartphone at home, immerse yourself in a forest, and breathe in the fresh air.
sentences.chinese: 另一种放松身心的方法是把手机留在家里，全身心投入到森林中，呼吸新鲜空气。

sentences.english: Forest bathing is the perfect tonic for the stresses of urban life.
sentences.chinese: 森林浴是缓解城市生活压力的绝佳良方。

sentences.english: Other life-improving ideas included things such as singing to reduce pain and fidgeting more to get away from our sedentary lives.
sentences.chinese: 其他改善生活的方法还包括唱歌缓解疼痛、多活动身体摆脱久坐的生活状态等。

sentences.english: But whatever therapy we choose to adopt, it seems any change to our lifestyle can help improve our body and mind.
sentences.chinese: 但无论我们选择哪种调节方式，只要改变生活习惯，似乎就能改善身心状态。
